originality.rationale: The inspected Bergou et al. 2023 theorem gives convergence-horizon bounds for fixed doubly perturbed systems, not the invariant fourth moment of a refreshed isotropic random hyperplane. The inspected Gower-Richtarik 2015 Gaussian Kaczmarz section contains the known expected squared-error rate but not independent response noise or stationary cumulant attenuation. The independent-response factor 3/(2d+1) paired with time-average correlation factor 2d-1 was not found in inspected primary text, relevant indexed records or close scientific variants; unpublished thermostat moment closures and one inaccessible 2014 full paper remain material publication-priority risks.
residual_risks: The Agaskar-Wang-Lu 2014 full text was not retrievable (HTTP 429), so its appendices cannot be ruled out by direct inspection.
Other indexed or unindexed Kac-type thermostatted random-coordinate renewal models might contain an equivalent fourth-order equilibrium closure; searches did not locate a decisive comparison.
The formulas are exact only under uniform spherical directions and fresh independent responses; no generalization to frozen/anisotropic data is asserted.

value.rationale: Fresh non-Gaussian equation measurements naturally arise in noisy row-action solvers, while fixed-system squared-error guarantees cannot diagnose invariant shape. The exact dimension factor 3/(2d+1) measures loss of excess kurtosis despite unchanged coordinate variance, and the exact factor 2d-1 quantifies concomitant autocorrelation cost. Together they provide a meaningful exact benchmark for interpreting Gaussian-looking numerical iterates and effective sample size, not a mere numerical lookup or arbitrary slice.
